verdict.rationale: Pipedream's own materials call it "low-code": common actions use pre-built components across thousands of integrated apps, and workflows can be tested by clicking "Send Test Event." However, the evidence never explicitly describes a visual drag-and-drop editor for multi-step workflows, and community comments frame it as "Zapier but for developers" and "more low level," with custom code positioned for anything beyond common actions. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of a visual workflow editor, evidence of no-code multi-step chaining (branching, data mapping between steps), and independent hands-on corroboration from non-developer ops users.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can build multi-step workflows in a visual editor without writing code

citations.quote: Pipedream is "low-code" in the best way: you can use pre-built components when you're performing common actions, but you can write custom code when you need to.
